spec_match.rationale: The calc(alpha * k) token-derivation pattern and the point that scaling preserves an already-translucent brand are correct applications of the spec, with a labelled best-available fallback chain.

interactive.rationale: The brand picker re-derives everything, but the four token tiles never show their tint in ANY browser: the checkerboard ::before (z-index:-1) and the derived background sit on the same isolated .fill element, and negative-z pseudo-elements paint ABOVE their element's own background — pixel-verified (tiles sample as bare checkerboard while the scrim with the identical inline background renders 114,133,252).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The blurb promises 'change the brand color and the entire derived palette re-tints live', but the tile row — the palette's main visualisation — visibly never tints.

edge_cases.rationale: Three-tier fallback (alpha() → rgb(from …) → plain rgba) is labelled at each tier, and the decl line prints both the derivation and the resolved computed value.

references.rationale: ChromeStatus 5070160203481088 (verified) and the css-color-5 relative-alpha anchor are linked.

conformance.rationale: The shared suite proves the real alpha() contract; its failures in this Chromium 141 session are environment-expected (alpha() unshipped here).

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI: fallback banner, scrim/ring/disabled component rendering, and resolved read-back verified with clean console (fonts.googleapis.com failure environmental); the tile-occlusion bug was pinned down by pixel sampling; the brand picker was not driven interactively.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts sample only the disabled button's computed background, which is why the broken tiles went unnoticed — the page's own telemetry cannot see its main visual.

design_system.rationale: Variables and structure are right, but the tile paint-order defect leaves the demo's core surfaces rendering as bare checkerboard in every browser.

accessibility.rationale: Tile captions carry the token names/factors as text, the scrim is aria-hidden, the focus-ring input is labelled, and the disabled button pairs disabled with aria-disabled.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Harness-validated ok/ok recorded in responsive-support.json (2026-07-24) and the auto-fill tile grid adapts; the tile bug affects both classes equally; this session's own 360px CLI capture is inconclusive due to the headless min-width clamp.

openQuestions.title: Fix the token tiles' paint order so the derived tint is visible
openQuestions.detail: `.tile .fill` is position:relative + isolation:isolate and carries BOTH the opaque checkerboard ::before (z-index:-1) and the derived background. In CSS painting order, negative-z descendants render above the element's own background, so the checkerboard fully occludes the tint — in native alpha() browsers too. Smallest fix: split like alpha-lab's swatches (checkerboard on the parent .tile/.fill, tint on a child div), or drop isolation and paint the tint on a ::after. Pixel evidence: tile fills sample (244,243,238) while the scrim with the identical background samples (114,133,252).

openQuestions.title: Extend the telemetry assert to a tile fill
openQuestions.detail: The existing assert samples the disabled button, which renders fine, so the broken tiles were invisible to telemetry. Also assert a computed background on the first tile's fill (or its replacement child) so a regression of the paint fix is caught in production.

summary: The design-system story and fallback chain are sound, and the in-context component (scrim, focus ring, disabled fill) genuinely re-tints — but the page's headline visual, the four derived-token tiles, has never displayed a tint in any browser because the checkerboard pseudo-element paints above the fill's own background; fix it in place with the smallest patch and add a tile-level telemetry assert. Verified with headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI (screenshots, DOM, pixel sampling proving tiles unpainted vs the identically-styled scrim, clean console); interaction not driven in this environment.
